metadata.scenario_context: Adam has won a scholarship to study at a prestigious university. His friends plan to hold a celebration party in his honor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from USA strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Iran strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of buying a bottle of champagne as a gift for Adam's celebration.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Adam's scholarship award celebration.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: Omar, I was thinking, for Adam's celebration, we should get him a really nice gift. What do you think about buying a bottle of champagne?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: Champagne sounds like a great idea, Kelly. But, I was thinking, maybe something more personal, like a framed photo or a book by his favorite author. My parents always taught me that a thoughtful gift is more important than an expensive one.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kelly
shared_prefix.message: Uh, that's a nice idea, but I'm not sure... I mean, champagne is classy, you know? And it's not just about the price. Anyway, speaking of parents, do you think one of the main goals in life is to make them proud?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Omar
shared_prefix.message: Actually, in our culture, making parents proud is NOT just one of the main goals, it's THE main goal. Properly speaking, a child's success is measured by how much they honor their family. Your way of thinking, where individual desires come first, is... naive. In our way, family is everything, and we don't just do things for personal gain. NO, it's about bringing pride to our parents, and that's what truly matters.
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: Well, I... I don't know if I agree with that. I mean, I love my parents, but I don't think making them proud is my main goal. That sounds kind of... suffocating. I want to make myself happy, you know? And, uh, what about Adam's celebration? Are we getting back to that or...?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: That's your perspective, Kelly. For me, making my parents proud is what drives me. It's not about being suffocated, it's about respect and honor. Anyway, yes, Adam's celebration. I think a thoughtful gift, like a personalized plaque or a book, would be more meaningful than just champagne. It shows we put effort into it, like my parents taught me.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I still think champagne is a great idea, it's *classic* for celebrations. And, honestly, I don't think my parents' pride is my main motivation. I mean, I want to do well for myself, not just to impress them. Can we please just decide on the champagne?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Omar
turns.message: I understand why you like the champagne idea, Kelly, but I still think something more personal would be better. As for your motivation, I respect your view, but for me, my parents' pride will always be my main goal. Let's compromise on the gift, how about a nice watch or a framed photo with a heartfelt message? That way, we show Adam we care and put thought into it.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kelly
turns.message: I... guess that's okay. A watch or a framed photo could work. But I'm still not convinced that making parents proud is the most important thing. I don't think that's what drives me, at all. Anyway, let's just go with the watch, I suppose. GOOD BYE!
turns.label: Acceptance

positive.mediator_utterance: Both Kelly and Omar, it's important to remember that while our cultural backgrounds may differ, we share the common goal of expressing appreciation for Adam's celebration. Let's explore how we can combine our unique perspectives to create a thoughtful and meaningful gift, rather than focusing on personal or cultural differences.
